docs.text: Rhema ¶ Rhema is a language for writing mathematics questions. A file describes a kind of question as a grammar: what shapes it may take, how hard it is, what its answer is and how it reads. The rhema compiler checks the file and writes the questions out for WeBWorK. # The smallest useful question: the sum of two numbers. synth value on E synth latex on E start E E -> integer_between ( 10 , 99 ) "+" integer_between ( 10 , 99 ) { value = $1 . value + $3 . value latex = str ( $1 . value ) ++ " + " ++ str ( $3 . value ) } prompt "What is [` {E.latex} `]?" answer E . value $ rhema run first.rhm --count 2 1. What is [`82 + 40`]? answer: 122 2. What is [`83 + 52`]? answer: 135 The question and its answer come from the same tree, so they cannot disagree. Difficulty is a budget the grammar spends exactly, chosen when the questions are generated. Grammars import one another, and a file can describe a whole assignment, which compiles to the same paper every time. Install ¶ opam install rhema opam is the package manager of OCaml, the language rhema is written in. If you do not have it yet, Installing with opam starts from there. This installs version 0.2.0: the rhema command and a library of grammars for arithmetic, algebra, calculus, propositional logic, sets, vectors, complex numbers, sequences, linear algebra, counting, number theory and statistics. Note 0.2.0 was released on 2026-11-16. Until the opam repository has accepted it, the command above gives 0.1.1; opam update followed by opam upgrade rhema brings 0.2.0 once it is there. For VS Code, install Rhema Language from the Marketplace. It gives .rhm files highlighting, problems from rhema check as you type, and commands to run and compile; the source is in editors/vscode . Where to go next ¶ The tutorial Eight short chapters, from the file above to a complete assignment in WeBWorK. Every example on the site is checked by the compiler on each change to the repository. The rhema command Compiling, checking, running and listing files, and how imported files are found. The name ¶ RHM , the project Rhema belongs to, stands for Reversible Hierarchical Mathesis , with the motto Regula · Hierarchia · Mathesis . Reversible A parser reads text into a tree. RHM runs that direction backwards: it builds the tree first and writes the question from it, so the question and its answer are two readings of one object. The first version did this literally, running the Menhir parser's grammar in reverse; the letters R-H-M are Menhir read backwards without its vowels. Hierarchical Questions are trees of productions. Difficulty is a budget passed down the tree, results are computed back up it, and grammars compose into assignments by import. Mathesis After Leibniz's mathesis universalis , a universal method of reasoning by calculation: here, a method of producing mathematics questions by rule. Rhema (Greek ῥῆμα, that which is said, an utterance ) is the name of the language. Its letters sit inside RHM, and it names what a grammar does: it says a question. Authors ¶ Jingming Zhang, Jiaming Lei, Xiaobo Huang, Jiesen Long and Zhiyuan Li, at Beijing Normal-Hong Kong Baptist University ; see Authors . Rhema is free software under the MIT licence; the source is on GitHub .

docs.text: Changelog ¶ Rhema follows semantic versioning: the language's syntax, the builtin functions' names and arguments, and the rhema command's options are the public interface. A breaking change raises the major version; a deprecation is announced one version before the removal. Unreleased ¶ Mistakes. A grammar can declare a mistake students make, mistake NAME "what the student does" , and say in a production what such a student computes, with a line mistake NAME ATTRIBUTE = EXPRESSION . After a question is built its tree is evaluated again under each mistake. A question in which a mistake changes the working and still gives the right answers is built afresh, so wrong working is never marked right; rhema run lists what each mistake leads to under the answer. Formulas are compared as functions. See chapter 9 of the tutorial and "Mistakes" in the language reference. Four library grammars declare mistakes: calculus.rhm (a product differentiated factor by factor, the chain rule left out, a quotient differentiated top and bottom), complex.rhm ( i squared taken to be 1, a minus sign kept from the imaginary part), boolean.rhm (a conditional with a false antecedent taken to be false, "or" read as exclusive) and the polynomial expansions (each term raised to the power on its own). Their papers change where a question hid a mistake: such a question is replaced, and the draws after it move. On a 500-question paper the first different question is number 245 for calculus.rhm derivatives, 67 for complex.rhm and 25 for boolean.rhm ; integrals, factorings and expansions are the same questions as in 0.2.0. A derivative answer of calculus.rhm is the same function as before and is sometimes written differently in PG. Failures end with a message. Several things a grammar can ask for ended the command with OCaml's Fatal error: exception ... and status 2. Each now stops with a message of one line and status 1: a name that is not a variable name given to polynomial_variable , polynomial_constant , polynomial_linear , polynomial_quadratic , formula_to_polynomial or one of the four functions that solve an equation; a zero divisor met inside differentiate or formula_substitute ; a negative size for matrix_identity ; an equation, or text holding a blank, that reaches an answer through cond , which rhema run listed and the PG writer stopped on. Whatever else is raised while a paper is generated or written is reported the same way. Generators draw from a range of any width. A range of more than 1073741823 values, such as integer(10) or integer_between(0, 2000000000) , ended in the same fatal error. It is now drawn from; integer(DIGITS) takes up to 18 digits and says so beyond. A narrower range is drawn exactly as before. Exact numbers no longer wrap round. A number is a fraction of two 63-bit integers, and a sum or product that did not fit gave a wrong number without a word, or, as in polynomial_power(polynomial_linear(1, 2, "x"), 100) , a stack overflow. Every operation is now checked; one that does not fit stops the question like a division by zero, with "a number grew too large to be kept exact". No question of the library is affected: its output is byte-identical. Static types. rhema check , and every command that reads a file, now infers the types every expression can have and reports a use that none of them allows: text in arithmetic, a number where a formula is wanted, a guard or requirement that is not a truth value, a budget update that is not a number, an equation as an answer, a child written $n where a value is wanted, a mistake line whose value the lines after it cannot take. Such a file used to pass the check and stop while generating. Nothing is declared: an attribute has the types its productions give it, by nonterminal, and a module's types cross an import. A use that only some types allow is still left to the engine, and so is everything that depends on the value (a whole number, a zero divisor, the shape of a matrix). See "Types" in the language reference. For a file without such a use nothing changes: every question type of the library, its set, and PG and LaTeX output are byte-identical. A file that generated before is refused now in two cases: a wrong type where nothing was ever evaluated (the unchosen branch of cond , the right side of and or or , a production no question reaches, the lines below a requirement that never holds, or a budget update, whose production the engine silently never chose); an answer that is an equation or text holding a blank, which rhema run listed and the PG writer could not write. rhema doc prints what each function takes and gives, and the builtins page of the site, generated from it, shows the same. mistake is now a reserved word. A grammar that used it as a name must rename it. A presentation at a terminal. When rhema writes to a terminal, compiling and running show the file, the assignment and the seed, the steps as they are reached, the progress of the generation and a summary of what was written; a problem is shown with its line of the file and a mark under the column. It all goes to standard error, and it is off when anything is redirected or piped, when CI is set and when PG goes to standard output, so what a program reads from rhema has not changed. --plain turns it off, --no-color (or NO_COLOR ) and --no-emoji tone it down, and -v / --verbose adds each question's derivation. It has a few jokes in it, and three hidden options ( --hello , --nailong , --coffee ). rhema try FILE . A session that shows the questions of a file one at a time and takes a command a line: a for the answer and what each mistake gives, = NUMBER to compare a number with the answer exactly (a number that is the answer of a declared mistake is told so), BUDGET = N , question NAME and seed N to change what is generated, t and pg to look at the derivation and the PG, and how for the rhema run command that prints the questions shown so far. A session shows exactly the questions that command does. It reads standard input, from a terminal or not. A missing name is asked for, at a terminal. A file of sets run without --run , a --run that names no set and a --question that names no question list the file's own names and ask which is meant. The answer is a number or a name of the list, never a guess, and the run is the one the same command gives with that name on it. Without somebody to ask (a pipe, a redirection, --plain ) these are the errors they were. Hints. An unknown option or command is reported with the one it is nearest to: unknown option --studnt (did you mean --student?) . Changed. --count with a negative number is an error of the command line (status 2); it was rhema: error: List.init . The "not run through WeBWorK" line of the summary is said only where PG was written. In the OCaml library, the record Rhema_load.failure has a third field, kind , which says whether a failure is of the syntax, of the meaning or of something else; code that builds such a record must give it. 0.2.0 (2026-11-16) ¶ The library grows from 27 grammar files to 46, seven of the new question types scale with the budget, and a paper can be written as LaTeX or PDF as well as WeBWorK PG. Coming from 0.1.1: true and false are now reserved words. A grammar that used either as a name must rename it; nothing else in the language or the command changed meaning. The 27 grammar files of 0.1.1 ask the same questions for the same seed (compared on 30 questions of each question type and on the library's set). Four of them write some answers differently in PG, so that WeBWorK grades them correctly: arithmetic.rhm and sequence.rhm (whole numbers and fractions of 1000 or more), set.rhm (unions without brackets around their parts) and logic_forms.rhm (propositions with their own context). The entries below give the reasons. A paper to print: LaTeX and PDF output. rhema FILE -o OUT.tex writes the same questions as a LaTeX document, and -o OUT.pdf compiles it with a TeX engine found on the machine ( pdflatex , xelatex , lualatex , tectonic , or the one RHEMA_LATEX names). --answers adds an answer key on a last page and --title sets the title. A set keeps its labels and headings, a blank becomes a rule to write on, and a formula too wide for the line is scaled down to it. The same assignment and student give the same questions as the .pg file. An output with any other extension is WeBWorK PG, as before. Seven question types scale with the budget. partial_fractions.rhm , taylor.rhm , inequality.rhm , partial_derivatives.rhm , row_reduction.rhm , base_conversion.rhm and definite_integral.rhm refused every budget above 3. They now go on to 8, building the question from priced parts: more factors and constants, sums and products of series, sign charts of up to five factors, functions of two variables with sin, cos and e, matrices of up to six columns and null spaces of dimension two and three, sums and differences across number bases, and integrals of sums of pieces. Budgets 1 to 3 give the same questions as before, seed for seed. A budget above 8 is refused. DIFFICULTY_BUDGET.md section 12 has the prices and what a grammar written this way must get right. Builtins : polynomial_truncate(p, n) , the terms of a polynomial of degree at most n , and matrix_null_space(A) , the basis of a null space read off the reduced form, as the columns of a matrix. Fixed : the WeBWorK renderer of the Docker stack could restart for ever after Docker itself was restarted (exit code 140). Its process id file outlived the container, and a new process with the same id took itself for a running server. compose.yml now empties that file before the renderer starts. Seven more question types , fixed forms at prices 1 to 3: partial_fractions.rhm (the constants, one blank each), recurrence.rhm (terms, characteristic roots and closed forms, up to four blanks), taylor.rhm , row_reduction.rhm (rank, reduced row echelon form, a vector of a null space), base_conversion.rhm , trigonometry.rhm (exact values and equations, answered as plain values) and partial_derivatives.rhm (answers in x and y ). Each has a test that checks its answers independently, and the teacher workspace lists them. pg_variables : a grammar names the variables of its formula answers, as a let of the file or as an attribute of the start symbol, so an answer that holds only one of them is entered in a blank that knows all. Builtins : base_digits(n, b) , a whole number written in base 2 to 16, and base_number(n, b) , the number with those digits in decimal, for answers in binary and octal. Fixed : a whole-number answer of 1000 or more accepted its neighbours. WeBWorK compares numbers with a relative tolerance of one part in a thousand, so 5041 passed for 5040. Such an answer is now written Real(n)->cmp(tolType=>"absolute",tolerance=>0.5) ; smaller whole numbers stay bare numbers. This changes the PG written by arithmetic.rhm , counting.rhm , sequence.rhm and series.rhm for their large answers, and by any grammar of your own with such answers. Fixed : a fraction answer whose numerator is 1000 or more accepted the neighbouring fractions, for the same reason: 4923/4 passed for 4922/4. Such an answer is now written Compute("p/q")->cmp(tolType=>"absolute",tolerance=>1/(2q)) , half a step of its denominator; a decimal typed in its place must be right to within that. Smaller fractions stay Formula('p/q') . This changes the PG of arithmetic.rhm for its large answers, and of a few answers of definite_integral.rhm and statistics.rhm . Fixed : WeBWorK could not read a proposition answer that holds a variable other than p and q , the two its Boolean context knows ("Variable 'r' is not defined in this context"); most rewriting questions of logic_forms.rhm were affected. A proposition answer is now written with a copy of the Boolean context that declares its variables and those named by pg_variables , so a grammar need not set context "Boolean" for it. tools/validate_webwork_renderer.py now compiles ten questions for each case and has WeBWorK build their answer evaluators, which is where such a fault shows. exactly(N) : a whole number graded that way whatever its size; base_conversion.rhm uses it for its binary and octal answers. Blanks in text : blank(VALUE) and blank_wide(VALUE, COLUMNS) make an answer blank that is joined to a production's text with ++ , so forms with different numbers of blanks can share a grammar and one blank can have a width of its own. A file that calls blank needs no answer line; an answer line together with blanks in the text is refused. analytic_geometry.rhm now asks for the centre and the radius of a circle in two blanks. Formulas in any variables : a formula answer with variables other than x is written with a context that declares them, so partial derivatives can be asked; before, such a problem did not compile in WeBWorK. formula_value gives the exact number a formula without variables comes to. π and exact values : formula_pi() , and exact_sin , exact_cos , exact_tan at multiples of π/6 and π/4. plain(VALUE) : an answer graded with the trigonometric, hyperbolic, logarithm and exponential functions switched off, so a question cannot be typed back as its own answer. exponential_log.rhm uses it for the value of a logarithm, where log(625)/log(5) used to be accepted. Fixed : a fraction in a formula is bracketed as a divisor and under a power, x/(2/3) and (2/3)^2 ; they were written x/2/3 and 2/3^2 , which WeBWorK reads as other numbers. No library grammar was affected. Language : true and false are the two truth values (both are now reserved words; a grammar that used either as a name must rename it). Language : a local name in a production, let NAME = EXPR inside the braces. It is computed after the children are built, is visible to the lines below it, and is not carried by the node, so it needs no synth . A name that would hide an attribute, a random or a file-level let is refused. Points : point2(x, y) , point3(x, y, z) and point_latex . A point answer is entered as (3, -2) and graded as a point in any context; the grammar does not set one. analytic_geometry.rhm uses it in place of a text answer in the Point context. Matrices of any shape : matrix_row , matrix_column , matrix_stack , matrix_augment , matrix_rows , matrix_columns , and matrix_rref and matrix_rank by exact Gauss-Jordan elimination. The six grammars of the batch below are rewritten with these; they ask the same questions. Documentation : a tutorial page, Installing with opam , that goes from a machine without opam to a working rhema : installing opam, opam init , opam install rhema , updating, removing, and what to do when a step fails. VS Code extension in editors/vscode : highlighting, problems from rhema check as you type, Run and Compile commands, folding and snippets for .rhm files. Its tests check the grammar against the compiler's keywords and every .rhm file in the repository (CI job editor ), and drive the extension in VS Code against a real rhema . Published on the Visual Studio Marketplace as rhema.rhema-language (a preview). Fixed : a problem with a name, a child reference or a call was reported at the start of the equation or declaration holding it, so value = foo gave the column of value for "unknown name 'foo'". Every such message now points at the name itself. The parser records where each one is written ( At in rhema_ast.ml ); generation is unchanged. Six more question types , fixed forms at prices 1 to 3 and built answer first: definite_integral.rhm (integrals of polynomials and the areas they measure), derivative_applications.rhm (tangent lines, critical points, extreme values, intervals of increase), exponential_log.rhm , analytic_geometry.rhm (lines and circles; a point is answered as (3, -2) ), differential_equation.rhm (initial value problems, answered by a formula) and statistics.rhm . They use the existing builtins only, and each has a test that checks its answers independently. The teacher workspace lists them. Six new question types , all built answer first: counting.rhm (arrangements, selections and probabilities, with named questions counting and probability ), number_theory.rhm , series.rhm , limits.rhm , eigen.rhm and inequality.rhm . Each has a test that checks its answers independently. Builtins : factorial , choose , permutations , gcd , lcm , pow_mod and mod_inverse on whole numbers ( rhema_integers.ml , with overflow checks); number_latex , a number in LaTeX with fractions as \frac ; and the rays set_above and set_below , rendered (a, \infty) and (-infinity, a] . A union of sets is written A U B in PG without brackets around its parts. A leaf (a generator, a literal or a terminal) may be read as $n.value without a synth value declaration; anything else on a leaf is refused with a hint to write str($n.value) . Fixed : a polynomial with a negative leading term was printed as a difference, 9 - (5 \cdot x^{2} + 4 \cdot x) ; it is now -5 \cdot x^{2} + 4 \cdot x + 9 . Documentation site ( docs/ , mkdocs.yml ): a home page, an eight-chapter tutorial, the language reference with its grammar in EBNF, the command, the builtin functions (generated from rhema doc ), the library and difficulty budgets. Every example file is checked and run in CI, and the site must build without warnings. Fixed : distinct in a set counted two different named questions built on the same rule as repeats, and could confuse rules of two files at the same line; it now compares the question type and the rule's file too. rhema doc groups functions by value type ( matrix2 with the matrices, differentiate with the formulas, the generators on their own) and points to the website. The set listing no longer prints an empty budget list. CI : GitHub Actions builds the package from a clean export on OCaml 4.14 and 5, Linux and macOS, exactly as opam does, installs it into a prefix and runs the command; a second job builds the whole tree with every suite, the documentation examples and site, and the Python checks. 0.1.1 (2026-10-25) ¶ Packaging only. The classic generator and its PG parser, which need pprint and menhirCST , are built in the development profile only, so the package's tests no longer fail on a machine without them ( dune build -p rhema @runtest ). No change to the language or the command. 0.1.0 (2026-10-24) ¶ The first version with a name. Language : Rhema, files .rhm . Attribute grammars with inherited budgets and synthesized attributes; include ; import "file.rhm" as name with arguments at the boundary; question NAME { ... } blocks; set NAME { ... } declarations with budgets drawn fixed, from a list, or around a mean; pg_context / pg_width per question; {answer ...} blanks. Values : Number, Formula, Polynomial, Equation, Boolean, Matrix, Set, Vector, Complex, with their builtin functions ( rhema doc ). Difficulty : every library grammar spends a cost budget exactly; --set cost=N ; sets fix the mean of a part. Command : rhema FILE.rhm [-o OUT.pg] , check , run , list , doc ; GNU error format and exit codes; -I and RHEMA_PATH ; one assignment is one paper, --student for a student's own. Library : 24 question grammars, 2 grammar libraries, 1 example set file, installed to share/rhema by dune install . Layout : generator/rhema/{lib,bin,test} , generator/stdlib , generator/grammars for the user's own files. Packaging : opam metadata in generator/dune-project (generated rhema.opam , MIT, tests run with --with-test ); RELEASING.md describes tagging, the source archive and the opam-repository entry.

A session that shows the questions of a file one at a time and takes a command a line: a for the answer and what each mistake gives, = NUMBER to compare a number with the answer exactly (a number that is the answer of a declared mistake is told so), BUDGET = N , question NAME and seed N to change what is generated, t and pg to look at the derivation and the PG, and how for the rhema run command that prints the questions shown so far. A session shows exactly the questions that command does. It reads standard input, from a terminal or not. A missing name is asked for, at a terminal. A file of sets run without --run , a --run that names no set and a --question that names no question list the file's own names and ask which is meant. The answer is a number or a name of the list, never a guess, and the run is the one the same command gives with that name on it. Without somebody to ask (a pipe, a redirection, --plain ) these are the errors they were. Hints. An unknown option or command is reported with the one it is nearest to: unknown option --studnt (did you mean --student?) . Changed. --count with a negative number is an error of the command line (status 2); it was rhema: error: List.init . The "not run through WeBWorK" line of the summary is said only where PG was written. In the OCaml library, the record Rhema_load.failure has a third field, kind , which says whether a failure is of the syntax, of the meaning or of something else; code that builds such a record must give it.

docs.text: The library grows from 27 grammar files to 46, seven of the new question types scale with the budget, and a paper can be written as LaTeX or PDF as well as WeBWorK PG. Coming from 0.1.1: true and false are now reserved words. A grammar that used either as a name must rename it; nothing else in the language or the command changed meaning. The 27 grammar files of 0.1.1 ask the same questions for the same seed (compared on 30 questions of each question type and on the library's set). Four of them write some answers differently in PG, so that WeBWorK grades them correctly: arithmetic.rhm and sequence.rhm (whole numbers and fractions of 1000 or more), set.rhm (unions without brackets around their parts) and logic_forms.rhm (propositions with their own context). The entries below give the reasons. A paper to print: LaTeX and PDF output. rhema FILE -o OUT.tex writes the same questions as a LaTeX document, and -o OUT.pdf compiles it with a TeX engine found on the machine ( pdflatex , xelatex , lualatex , tectonic , or the one RHEMA_LATEX names). --answers adds an answer key on a last page and --title sets the title. A set keeps its labels and headings, a blank becomes a rule to write on, and a formula too wide for the line is scaled down to it. The same assignment and student give the same questions as the .pg file. An output with any other extension is WeBWorK PG, as before. Seven question types scale with the budget. partial_fractions.rhm , taylor.rhm , inequality.rhm , partial_derivatives.rhm , row_reduction.rhm , base_conversion.rhm and definite_integral.rhm refused every budget above 3. They now go on to 8, building the question from priced parts: more factors and constants, sums and products of series, sign charts of up to five factors, functions of two variables with sin, cos and e, matrices of up to six columns and null spaces of dimension two and three, sums and differences across number bases, and integrals of sums of pieces. Budgets 1 to 3 give the same questions as before, seed for seed. A budget above 8 is refused. DIFFICULTY_BUDGET.md section 12 has the prices and what a grammar written this way must get right. Builtins : polynomial_truncate(p, n) , the terms of a polynomial of degree at most n , and matrix_null_space(A) , the basis of a null space read off the reduced form, as the columns of a matrix. Fixed : the WeBWorK renderer of the Docker stack could restart for ever after Docker itself was restarted (exit code 140). Its process id file outlived the container, and a new process with the same id took itself for a running server. compose.yml now empties that file before the renderer starts. Seven more question types , fixed forms at prices 1 to 3: partial_fractions.rhm (the constants, one blank each), recurrence.rhm (terms, characteristic roots and closed forms, up to four blanks), taylor.rhm , row_reduction.rhm (rank, reduced row echelon form, a vector of a null space), base_conversion.rhm , trigonometry.rhm (exact values and equations, answered as plain values) and partial_derivatives.rhm (answers in x and y ). Each has a test that checks its answers independently, and the teacher workspace lists them. pg_variables : a grammar names the variables of its formula answers, as a let of the file or as an attribute of the start symbol, so an answer that holds only one of them is entered in a blank that knows all. Builtins : base_digits(n, b) , a whole number written in base 2 to 16, and base_number(n, b) , the number with those digits in decimal, for answers in binary and octal. Fixed : a whole-number answer of 1000 or more accepted its neighbours. WeBWorK compares numbers with a relative tolerance of one part in a thousand, so 5041 passed for 5040. Such an answer is now written Real(n)->cmp(tolType=>"absolute",tolerance=>0.5) ; smaller whole numbers stay bare numbers. This changes the PG written by arithmetic.rhm , counting.rhm , sequence.rhm and series.rhm for their large answers, and by any grammar of your own with such answers. Fixed : a fraction answer whose numerator is 1000 or more accepted the neighbouring fractions, for the same reason: 4923/4 passed for 4922/4. Such an answer is now written Compute("p/q")->cmp(tolType=>"absolute",tolerance=>1/(2q)) , half a step of its denominator; a decimal typed in its place must be right to within that. Smaller fractions stay Formula('p/q') . This changes the PG of arithmetic.rhm for its large answers, and of a few answers of definite_integral.rhm and statistics.rhm . Fixed : WeBWorK could not read a proposition answer that holds a variable other than p and q , the two its Boolean context knows ("Variable 'r' is not defined in this context"); most rewriting questions of logic_forms.rhm were affected. A proposition answer is now written with a copy of the Boolean context that declares its variables and those named by pg_variables , so a grammar need not set context "Boolean" for it. tools/validate_webwork_renderer.py now compiles ten questions for each case and has WeBWorK build their answer evaluators, which is where such a fault shows. exactly(N) : a whole number graded that way whatever its size; base_conversion.rhm uses it for its binary and octal answers. Blanks in text : blank(VALUE) and blank_wide(VALUE, COLUMNS) make an answer blank that is joined to a production's text with ++ , so forms with different numbers of blanks can share a grammar and one blank can have a width of its own. A file that calls blank needs no answer line; an answer line together with blanks in the text is refused. analytic_geometry.rhm now asks for the centre and the radius of a circle in two blanks. Formulas in any variables : a formula answer with variables other than x is written with a context that declares them, so partial derivatives can be asked; before, such a problem did not compile in WeBWorK. formula_value gives the exact number a formula without variables comes to. π and exact values : formula_pi() , and exact_sin , exact_cos , exact_tan at multiples of π/6 and π/4. plain(VALUE) : an answer graded with the trigonometric, hyperbolic, logarithm and exponential functions switched off, so a question cannot be typed back as its own answer. exponential_log.rhm uses it for the value of a logarithm, where log(625)/log(5) used to be accepted. Fixed : a fraction in a formula is bracketed as a divisor and under a power, x/(2/3) and (2/3)^2 ; they were written x/2/3 and 2/3^2 , which WeBWorK reads as other numbers. No library grammar was affected. Language : true and false are the two truth values (both are now reserved words; a grammar that used either as a name must rename it). Language : a local name in a production, let NAME = EXPR inside the braces. It is computed after the children are built, is visible to the lines below it, and is not carried by the node, so it needs no synth . A name that would hide an attribute, a random or a file-level let is refused. Points : point2(x, y) , point3(x, y, z) and point_latex . A point answer is entered as (3, -2) and graded as a point in any context; the grammar does not set one. analytic_geometry.rhm uses it in place of a text answer in the Point context. Matrices of any shape : matrix_row , matrix_column , matrix_stack , matrix_augment , matrix_rows , matrix_columns , and matrix_rref and matrix_rank by exact Gauss-Jordan elimination. The six grammars of the batch below are rewritten with these; they ask the same questions. Documentation : a tutorial page, Installing with opam , that goes from a machine without opam to a working rhema : installing opam, opam init , opam install rhema , updating, removing, and what to do when a step fails. VS Code extension in editors/vscode : highlighting, problems from rhema check as you type, Run and Compile commands, folding and snippets for .rhm files. Its tests check the grammar against the compiler's keywords and every .rhm file in the repository (CI job editor ), and drive the extension in VS Code against a real rhema . Published on the Visual Studio Marketplace as rhema.rhema-language (a preview). Fixed : a problem with a name, a child reference or a call was reported at the start of the equation or declaration holding it, so value = foo gave the column of value for "unknown name 'foo'". Every such message now points at the name itself. The parser records where each one is written ( At in rhema_ast.ml ); generation is unchanged. Six more question types , fixed forms at prices 1 to 3 and built answer first: definite_integral.rhm (integrals of polynomials and the areas they measure), derivative_applications.rhm (tangent lines, critical points, extreme values, intervals of increase), exponential_log.rhm , analytic_geometry.rhm (lines and circles; a point is answered as (3, -2) ), differential_equation.rhm (initial value problems, answered by a formula) and statistics.rhm . They use the existing builtins only, and each has a test that checks its answers independently. The teacher workspace lists them. Six new question types , all built answer first: counting.rhm (arrangements, selections and probabilities, with named questions counting and probability ), number_theory.rhm , series.rhm , limits.rhm , eigen.rhm and inequality.rhm . Each has a test that checks its answers independently. Builtins : factorial , choose , permutations , gcd , lcm , pow_mod and mod_inverse on whole numbers ( rhema_integers.ml , with overflow checks); number_latex , a number in LaTeX with fractions as \frac ; and the rays set_above and set_below , rendered (a, \infty) and (-infinity, a] . A union of sets is written A U B in PG without brackets around its parts. A leaf (a generator, a literal or a terminal) may be read as $n.value without a synth value declaration; anything else on a leaf is refused with a hint to write str($n.value) . Fixed : a polynomial with a negative leading term was printed as a difference, 9 - (5 \cdot x^{2} + 4 \cdot x) ; it is now -5 \cdot x^{2} + 4 \cdot x + 9 . Documentation site ( docs/ , mkdocs.yml ): a home page, an eight-chapter tutorial, the language reference with its grammar in EBNF, the command, the builtin functions (generated from rhema doc ), the library and difficulty budgets. Every example file is checked and run in CI, and the site must build without warnings. Fixed : distinct in a set counted two different named questions built on the same rule as repeats, and could confuse rules of two files at the same line; it now compares the question type and the rule's file too. rhema doc groups functions by value type ( matrix2 with the matrices, differentiate with the formulas, the generators on their own) and points to the website. The set listing no longer prints an empty budget list. CI : GitHub Actions builds the package from a clean export on OCaml 4.14 and 5, Linux and macOS, exactly as opam does, installs it into a prefix and runs the command; a second job builds the whole tree with every suite, the documentation examples and site, and the Python checks.

Packaging only. The classic generator and its PG parser, which need pprint and menhirCST , are built in the development profile only, so the package's tests no longer fail on a machine without them ( dune build -p rhema @runtest ). No change to the language or the command.

The first version with a name. Language : Rhema, files .rhm . Attribute grammars with inherited budgets and synthesized attributes; include ; import "file.rhm" as name with arguments at the boundary; question NAME { ... } blocks; set NAME { ... } declarations with budgets drawn fixed, from a list, or around a mean; pg_context / pg_width per question; {answer ...} blanks. Values : Number, Formula, Polynomial, Equation, Boolean, Matrix, Set, Vector, Complex, with their builtin functions ( rhema doc ). Difficulty : every library grammar spends a cost budget exactly; --set cost=N ; sets fix the mean of a part. Command : rhema FILE.rhm [-o OUT.pg] , check , run , list , doc ; GNU error format and exit codes; -I and RHEMA_PATH ; one assignment is one paper, --student for a student's own. Library : 24 question grammars, 2 grammar libraries, 1 example set file, installed to share/rhema by dune install . Layout : generator/rhema/{lib,bin,test} , generator/stdlib , generator/grammars for the user's own files. Packaging : opam metadata in generator/dune-project (generated rhema.opam , MIT, tests run with --with-test ); RELEASING.md describes tagging, the source archive and the opam-repository entry.

Visual Question Builder ¶ The visual builder creates a new Rhema specification by composing existing mathematical library operations. It does not execute user-supplied Python or OCaml, introduce a second mathematical engine, or require an AI API key. Create a Question Type ¶ Select Create question type and enter a new .rhm filename. Choose Visual builder . Rhema source still offers the original basic, blank and existing-file starting points. Choose an example or Empty definition . Examples cover polynomial/calculus, Boolean evaluation, sequences, vectors, complex numbers and sets. Define random integer, nonzero-integer or Boolean parameters. Add mathematical steps. Each step can use literals and compatible values from earlier steps. Names are references, not executable code. Write the question text. Use Insert value for mathematical objects and parameters. These inserts appear as {name} in the editor and are rendered as mathematics in the question. Select the standard answer under Use result from . Conditions can reference true/false results and require either true or false. Select Check . This runs the real Rhema checker and two deterministic sample generations. It is not a proof that all possible random assignments satisfy every constraint. Enter an optional student ID and select Generate questions . The right panel contains real WeBWorK rendering and answer checking, generated Rhema, PGML and the generation tree. WeBWorK requires the existing Docker renderer. Select Save question type , then Open in Configure for the ordinary parameter-based generation workflow. The result is a new question type in Question library , not a form preset. My presets remains the place for saved Configure settings. Compose a Different Question ¶ The polynomial example constructs p , differentiates it into d , and evaluates d at random point k . To ask about a squared polynomial instead: Change the second step to Power of polynomial . Keep p as its input and set the exponent to 2. Leave the third step as Evaluate polynomial at a point , using d and k . Change the wording to Given P(x) = {p}, find the square of P({k}). Check, generate and save. The question wording must describe the actual mathematical steps. The builder checks references and types, but does not interpret natural-language wording to prove that it asks for the selected answer. Edit and Protect Existing Work ¶ Select a saved visual question type in the library, then Visual definition . Its definition can be edited and saved again. Updates require the source revision loaded by the editor; stale tabs cannot overwrite later source changes. Previous source and definition versions are backed up before an update. Each visual type has two files: generator/grammars/<name>.rhm : executable Rhema specification; usable through Configure, source mode and the CLI. generator/grammars/.visual/<name>.rhm.json : structured definition and source revision, required to reopen Visual builder. Keep both files when sharing a visual question type. Renaming a .rhm file alone does not rename its visual definition. If its source is manually edited, the existing Rhema/Configure workflows remain available, but Visual builder refuses to overwrite the changed source. Arbitrary hand-written Rhema is not automatically converted back into a visual graph. Boundaries ¶ Only catalogued adapters to existing library functions are available. The catalog is defined in visual_library.py ; compilation and validation are in visual_builder.py . Extending an existing mathematical primitive requires a typed adapter, not another question-specific generator. This version composes acyclic mathematical steps with one answer. It does not provide a visual editor for arbitrary recursive productions or multi-part questions. Existing recursive .rhm grammars remain available in Configure and Source mode. Scalar number inputs are integers; exact fractions can be formed with the division operation. Variable names and variable-order strings are restricted to safe identifier-like text. Type compatibility is checked before compilation. Domain conditions such as matrix dimensions, invertibility, equation support and valid exponents are also checked by the existing mathematical libraries at generation time. Finite sets and general sets are distinguished: insertion accepts a finite set, while union/intersection/difference also accept intervals. Constraints can be unsatisfiable or too restrictive. A failed check does not relax them silently. Prefer constructive generation and suitable random ranges. Same specification, settings, implementation and student ID reproduce question content. Different IDs do not guarantee unique or equally difficult questions. Definition limits: 12 random parameters, 30 steps, 12 constraints, 2,000 prompt characters, and an answer width of 1-100. These limits keep editor and runtime work bounded. Local Tests ¶ python -m unittest tools.test_visual_builder node --test tools/test_visual_builder.js tools/test_pg_preview.js The Python suite exercises the real Rhema runtime in temporary folders, including every catalog adapter, source conflicts, deterministic generation, Configure interoperability and rollback after a failed metadata write. Browser rendering and live answer checking require WeBWorK and are additional integration checks.

The rhema command ¶ rhema FILE.rhm [-o OUT.pg] [options] compile FILE to WeBWorK PG rhema FILE.rhm -o OUT.tex | OUT.pdf the same questions as a paper rhema check FILE... check only rhema run FILE [options] show the questions and answers rhema try FILE [options] try the file out, a question at a time rhema list FILE the questions and sets FILE declares rhema doc [NAME] the builtin functions (or one of them) rhema --version | --help Compiling ¶ rhema FILE.rhm checks the file, generates questions and writes them as a WeBWorK problem file. The output is named after the input ( quiz.rhm gives quiz.pg ), or after the set with --run SET ; -o OUT.pg names it, and -o - writes to standard output. $ rhema calculus.rhm --question integral -o integral.pg $ rhema homework_set.rhm --run homework # homework.pg $ rhema homework_set.rhm --run quick --pg-dir out/ --pg-dir DIR , with --run , also writes one file per question, named question01.pg , question02.pg and so on. A paper: LaTeX and PDF ¶ The extension of the output says what is written. -o OUT.tex writes the same questions as a LaTeX document, and -o OUT.pdf compiles that document to a PDF: $ rhema homework_set.rhm --run homework -o homework.tex $ rhema homework_set.rhm --run homework -o homework.pdf --answers $ rhema calculus.rhm --count 10 --set cost=6 -o quiz.pdf --title "Quiz 2" The paper has a title, the questions numbered as the set numbers them ( 1(a). , 2. ), the headings of its parts, and a rule to write on where each answer blank stands. The same assignment and the same --student give the same questions in all three formats. --answers An answer key on a last page: one entry for each question, one answer for each blank. --title TEXT The paper's title. The default is the set's name, the assignment's with --assignment , or the file's name. A .pdf needs a TeX engine on the machine. rhema uses the first of pdflatex , xelatex , lualatex and tectonic that it finds, or the one the environment variable RHEMA_LATEX names. When there is none, or the engine fails, it says so, writes no PDF and leaves the LaTeX beside where the PDF would be. The document needs only amsmath , amssymb , graphicx and geometry . The LaTeX is meant to be edited. Every question is set through four commands defined at the top of the file ( hemaquestion , hemablank , hemaheading , hemamath ), so another layout is a change to those lines. hemamath keeps a formula whole and scales it down when it is wider than the line, so that a long derivative or a wide matrix stays on the page. In the text of a question, [`...`] and [``...``] are mathematics, two spaces at the end of a line are a line break, and every other character is printed as it is. Other PGML markup, such as *bold* , is not interpreted. Options ¶ --question NAME One of the file's named questions. The default is main , the question the file declares outside any question block. --run SET The set SET declared in the file. A set names its own questions, counts and budgets, so --question , --count and --set do not apply. --count N How many questions to generate, when not running a set. Default 5. --assignment NAME The assignment this paper is. One assignment is one paper: generating it again gives the same questions. The default is the set's name, or FILE:QUESTION . --student ID A paper of this student's own for the assignment, the same every time and different from the other students' and from the assignment's. --set NAME=VALUE Start an inherited attribute of the question at VALUE , usually the difficulty budget: --set cost=6 . -I DIR Also look for imported and included files in DIR . --ast-out FILE , --visualization-out FILE Save the derivation trees as text, or as an interactive HTML page. In a terminal ¶ When rhema writes to a terminal, compiling and running show more than the result: the file, the assignment and the seed, the four steps as they are reached, the progress of the generation, and at the end how many questions were made and which files were written. A problem is shown with its line of the file and a mark under the column. All of this goes to standard error and none of it is part of the result. It is off whenever the output or the errors are redirected or piped, when the environment variable CI is set, and when PG is written to standard output; what an editor, a script or another program reads is the same as without it. --plain No presentation at a terminal either. --no-color No colors. The environment variable NO_COLOR does the same. --no-emoji Marks and the progress bar in ASCII. -v , --verbose Also print, on standard error, the derivation of each question: the rules that were accepted and the attribute values at each node. Being asked ¶ A command that cannot go on for want of a name asks for it, when there is somebody to ask: the presentation is on and the input is a terminal too. This happens in three cases: a file that holds only sets and no --run , a --run that names no set of the file, and a --question that names no question of it. $ rhema run homework_set.rhm homework_set.rhm: this file has no question of its own; it holds the sets homework, quick, run one with --run NAME [1] homework [2] quick Which set? A number or a name; Enter alone stops: 2 The same as giving --run quick. The answer is a number of the list or a name on it, and nothing else is taken for one: a name that is nearly right is asked for again. What follows is the run the same command gives with that name on it, the same paper and the same default output file. Enter alone, the end of the input, or three answers that are not on the list end the command with the error it gives everywhere else, and status 1. Hints ¶ An option or a command that is not known is reported with the one it is nearest to, when one is near: $ rhema run quiz.rhm --studnt 20261234 rhema: unknown option --studnt (did you mean --student?) $ rhema chek quiz.rhm rhema: 'chek' is neither a command nor a file (did you mean check?) A hint is only said. The command still stops with status 2. Trying a file out ¶ rhema try FILE shows the questions of a file one at a time and takes a command a line: look at the answer, compare a number with it, change a budget and see what the questions become. $ rhema try arithmetic.rhm -- main, cost = 12, digit = 4, seed 1851610664 1. What is the value of [`5 \div 6 - (8 - 65 + (3 - 7))`]? try> a answer: 371/6 try> cost = 3 -- main, cost = 3, digit = 4, seed 1851610664 1. What is the value of [`8033`]? try> 2. What is the value of [`4595`]? try> how rhema run arithmetic.rhm --set cost=3 --seed 1851610664 --count 2 Command What it does Enter alone, n The next question. a The answer, and what each mistake that can be made in the question leads to: the lines rhema run prints. = NUMBER Compares a number with the answer. Several answers are separated by ; . t The derivation: the rules accepted and the attribute values. pg The question as WeBWorK PG. how The command that prints the questions shown so far. question NAME Another question of the file. BUDGET = N Starts a budget at N , as --set BUDGET=N does. reset The budgets as the file sets them. seed N , seed Starts from seed N ; alone, from the seed rhema run derives. list The questions and budgets of the file. ? These commands. quit Ends the session. So does the end of the input. A session shows what a command would. The questions of a session are the questions of rhema run : the first one is the first question of rhema run FILE with the same options, and the Nth one since the last change is the Nth of the command how prints. To keep that true, changing the question, a budget or the seed starts again at question 1, and the line beginning with -- says where the session stands. A command that is refused, such as a budget the file does not have, changes nothing. = compares numbers, exactly. A whole number, a fraction ( 3/4 ) or a decimal ( 0.75 ) is compared with the answer as an exact number: 0.33 is not 1/3 . This is stricter than WeBWorK, which accepts a number within one part in a thousand. The reply is right , or not right , or, when the number is what one of the grammar's mistakes gives, the mistake: try> = 12 not right: this is the answer of the mistake forgot_sign (forgets the minus sign) The answer itself is not given away. An answer that is not a number (a formula, a set, a matrix) is not compared: when two of those are the same is for WeBWorK to say, and a shows the answer. docs.text: The extension of the output says what is written. -o OUT.tex writes the same questions as a LaTeX document, and -o OUT.pdf compiles that document to a PDF: $ rhema homework_set.rhm --run homework -o homework.tex $ rhema homework_set.rhm --run homework -o homework.pdf --answers $ rhema calculus.rhm --count 10 --set cost=6 -o quiz.pdf --title "Quiz 2" The paper has a title, the questions numbered as the set numbers them ( 1(a). , 2. ), the headings of its parts, and a rule to write on where each answer blank stands. The same assignment and the same --student give the same questions in all three formats. --answers An answer key on a last page: one entry for each question, one answer for each blank. --title TEXT The paper's title. The default is the set's name, the assignment's with --assignment , or the file's name. A .pdf needs a TeX engine on the machine. rhema uses the first of pdflatex , xelatex , lualatex and tectonic that it finds, or the one the environment variable RHEMA_LATEX names. When there is none, or the engine fails, it says so, writes no PDF and leaves the LaTeX beside where the PDF would be. The document needs only amsmath , amssymb , graphicx and geometry . The LaTeX is meant to be edited. Every question is set through four commands defined at the top of the file ( \rhemaquestion , \rhemablank , \rhemaheading , \rhemamath ), so another layout is a change to those lines. \rhemamath keeps a formula whole and scales it down when it is wider than the line, so that a long derivative or a wide matrix stays on the page. In the text of a question, [`...`] and [``...``] are mathematics, two spaces at the end of a line are a line break, and every other character is printed as it is. Other PGML markup, such as *bold* , is not interpreted.

docs.text: Difficulty budgets ¶ Every grammar in the library sets its difficulty the same way: a budget, an inherited attribute called cost , that the question spends exactly. Chapter 2 of the tutorial explains the mechanism; this page is about using it. What a budget pays for ¶ A production pays its price and divides the rest between its parts, and a leaf stands only where the rest of the budget buys it. Prices are chosen so that a harder operation costs more: in arithmetic.rhm a sum costs 1 and a quotient 4, and each digit beyond the first costs 1; in calculus.rhm a product costs 3 because it calls for the product rule, and a function of a compound costs 3 more than a function of x because it calls for the chain rule. The price of every grammar is in the library tables . Cost is not length. One budget buys questions of several sizes, so two questions at the same budget may look different and ask for the same amount of work. Grammars whose questions come in a few fixed forms (a dot product, a cross product, a unit vector) give each form a price and offer it only at exactly that budget. Choosing a budget ¶ The default in each file is a middle difficulty. For a single question type: $ rhema run boolean.rhm --set cost=6 # easy $ rhema run boolean.rhm --set cost=10 # medium, the default $ rhema run boolean.rhm --set cost=14 # hard Small budgets buy few different questions. For boolean.rhm , measured on 500 questions at each budget: Budget Distinct questions Answer true 4 34% 52% 6 63% 54% 8 87% 51% 10 97% 49% 14 100% 51% A set drawn at a budget where few questions are distinct will repeat itself, or fail under distinct , so stay above about 6 for this grammar. An assignment's difficulty is a mean ¶ For an assignment, fix the average rather than every question: 3 of calc . derivative ( cost ~ 6 spread 2 low 2 ) draws three budgets around 6 and adjusts them so that their mean is exactly 6: some easier, some harder, at a known level overall. rhema run reports the mean of each part. See chapter 7 of the tutorial. Measuring a grammar ¶ tools/rhema_difficulty.py in the repository measures what each budget buys: $ python3 tools/rhema_difficulty.py report generator/stdlib/boolean.rhm --at 6,10,14 $ python3 tools/rhema_difficulty.py levels generator/stdlib/boolean.rhm report prints, for each budget, the share of distinct questions, the share of the most common answer, the length of the displayed expression and the size of the derivation tree. levels suggests an easy, a medium and a hard budget: easy is the least budget at which at least half the questions are distinct, medium is the default, hard is as far above medium as easy is below. Giving your own grammar a budget ¶ Declare attribute cost = N split , with N a middle difficulty. Give each production a price with cost = -PRICE and a guard when cost >= PRICE ; give each leaf the guard when cost = 0 (or the price of the leaf, if a leaf has one). Make every budget spendable: from the smallest question upwards, every whole number must be the total price of some tree, or a node will receive a budget no production can take. Check with rhema run --set cost=N over a range of N ; a gap shows as no rule for 'E' fits .
