docs.text: Values and answers ¶ The answer to a differentiation question is a function, not a number. Rhema computes it, symbolically, from the same object the question shows. # The derivative of a x^n + b x. The coefficients are drawn once per question. random a = integer_between ( 2 , 9 ) random n = integer_between ( 2 , 6 ) random b = nonzero_integer_between ( - 9 , 9 ) let x = formula_variable ( "x" ) let f = formula_add ( formula_multiply ( formula_constant ( a ), formula_power ( x , n )), formula_multiply ( formula_constant ( b ), x )) let f_latex = formula_latex ( f ) synth derivative on Q start Q Q -> "derivative" { derivative = differentiate ( f , "x" ) } prompt "Differentiate [`f(x) = {f_latex} `] with respect to [`x`]." answer Q . derivative $ rhema run values.rhm --count 3 1. Differentiate [`f(x) = 5 \cdot x^{3} - 8 \cdot x`] with respect to [`x`]. answer: Formula(5*3*x^2-8) 2. Differentiate [`f(x) = 6 \cdot x^{6} - 8 \cdot x`] with respect to [`x`]. answer: Formula(6*6*x^5-8) 3. Differentiate [`f(x) = 5 \cdot x^{4} + 5 \cdot x`] with respect to [`x`]. answer: Formula(5*4*x^3+5) Values drawn once per question ¶ random a = integer_between ( 2 , 9 ) random n = integer_between ( 2 , 6 ) random b = nonzero_integer_between ( - 9 , 9 ) A random is drawn once for each question, before any tree is built, and has the same value everywhere it is used. Use one when several parts of a question must agree: the coefficients here, or the truth values of p , q and r in a logic question, which must be the same at every occurrence. random NAME = boolean draws true or false; the other draws are the four generators integer(DIGITS) , nonzero_integer(DIGITS) , integer_between(LOW, HIGH) and nonzero_integer_between(LOW, HIGH) , with whole-number literals as arguments. Values computed once per question ¶ let x = formula_variable ( "x" ) let f = formula_add ( formula_multiply ( formula_constant ( a ), formula_power ( x , n )), formula_multiply ( formula_constant ( b ), x )) let f_latex = formula_latex ( f ) A let is computed once per question, from the randoms and the lets above it. It may call any builtin function. {f_latex} in the prompt is replaced by its value, just as {E.latex} was replaced by an attribute. Types of value ¶ f is not text: it is a formula , a value the engine can differentiate, substitute into, compare and write out as LaTeX or for WeBWorK. Every attribute, random and let holds one of these: Value Made by Graded by WeBWorK as Number literals, arithmetic, generators an exact number, or a fraction Text strings, ++ , str , the *_latex functions (not an answer) Truth true , false , comparisons, and , or , not , random ... = boolean 1 or 0 Formula formula_* , differentiate , exact_sin and its like a formula, by equivalence, in x or in any variables Polynomial polynomial_* a formula Equation equation_* not directly: equation_solution_set gives a Set Boolean bool_* a proposition, by equivalence, in any variables Matrix matrix_* a matrix (Matrix context) Set set_* an interval or union (Interval context) Vector vector_* a vector (Vector context) Point point2 , point3 a point such as (3, -2) , in any context Complex complex a complex number (Complex context) The builtin functions are listed by value type, with what each takes and gives. A function given a value it cannot take is found by rhema check , before any question is generated, with a message that names both: values.rhm:8:76: error: formula_power takes a number as its second argument, but formula_constant(...) is a formula (This is what happens if the exponent is written formula_constant(n) : formula_power takes its exponent as a plain number. The reference says what the checker can and cannot tell: Types .) The answer is computed, not typed ¶ Q -> "derivative" { derivative = differentiate ( f , "x" ) } answer Q . derivative The prompt shows f ; the answer is differentiate(f, "x") . Both come from the one value f , so a question cannot be printed with one function and graded against the derivative of another. The answer is not simplified ( 5*3*x^2-8 rather than 15*x^2-8 ), and it does not need to be: WeBWorK compares formulas by evaluating them, so a student who types 15x^2 - 8 is marked right. docs.text: Into WeBWorK ¶ rhema compiles a file to a WeBWorK problem file ( .pg ), ready to upload to a course. Compiling ¶ $ rhema assignment.rhm --run week3 writes week3.pg in the current directory. The output is named after the set with --run , otherwise after the input file ( quiz.rhm gives quiz.pg ); -o NAME.pg names it, and -o - prints it. A single question type compiles the same way. --count says how many questions to put in the file: $ rhema values.rhm --count 10 -o derivatives.pg $ rhema questions.rhm --question sum --count 5 -o sums.pg What the file contains ¶ $ rhema assignment.rhm --run week3 -o - | head -13 DOCUMENT(); loadMacros("PGstandard.pl", "MathObjects.pl", "PGML.pl"); Context("Numeric"); BEGIN_PGML Sequences 1. An arithmetic sequence has first term [`a_1 = 0`] and common difference [`d = 5`]. (a) Find [`a_{14}`]. [_____]{65} (b) Find the sum of its first [`14`] terms. [_____]{455} It is ordinary PG: the macros it needs, the context, and the questions in PGML with their answers in the blanks. Questions that need a different context, such as a proposition to rewrite in the Boolean context, are put in their own PGML block with the context switched before it. One paper per assignment ¶ Compiling week3 again gives the same file, today or next term. The paper is fixed by the assignment's name, which is the set's name unless you give another: $ rhema assignment.rhm --run week3 --assignment "MATH2003 HW3" Two assignments with different names are different papers, even from the same file. Nothing about the paper depends on when or where it was compiled. A paper for each student ¶ When every student should have different numbers, name the student: $ rhema assignment.rhm --run week3 --student 2330026211 -o week3_2330026211.pg Each student's paper is fixed in the same way: the same student and assignment always give the same paper, so it can be regenerated for marking or a resit. Most assignments do not need this; one paper for the whole class is the default for a reason. One file per question ¶ $ rhema assignment.rhm --run week3 --pg-dir week3/ writes week3.pg and also week3/question01.pg , question02.pg and so on, for courses that prefer one problem per file. It holds the questions of week3.pg , the same ones: a paper is named by its assignment, not by its format. A PDF needs a TeX engine installed; see the command . Homework Sets Editor : create the set, or open an existing one. Library Browser : choose the course's local problems, browse to the uploaded files, and add them to the set. Open a problem as a student to check that it displays and accepts the answer. The files are plain text and can also be copied into the course's templates directory by anyone with access to the server. Before you upload ¶ rhema run shows exactly the questions and answers that will be in the file, so read the paper there first: $ rhema run assignment.rhm --run week3 That is everything a paper needs. docs.text: Builtin functions ¶ The functions an expression may call, grouped by the kind of value they work on. This page is generated from rhema doc , so it lists exactly what the compiler accepts, with the types each function takes and gives. Calling one with the wrong number of arguments, or with a value that cannot have a type it takes, is an error the checker reports ( Types ). Where text is taken, a number is written out. Numbers, text and rendering ¶ Functions on numbers and text, and the two that write operators with the right brackets. Function Takes Gives str text text A number written out as text; text is left as it is. paren text text Its argument with brackets around it. infix a child $n, text, a child $n text infix($1, "+", $3) : the two children joined by the operator text, bracketed as the precedence table requires. prefix text, a child $n text prefix("\neg", $2) : the operator text before the child, bracketed as the precedence table requires. cond truth value, any value, any value its second or third argument cond(c, a, b) : a when c is true, b otherwise. abs number number The absolute value of a number. min number, number number The smaller of two numbers. max number, number number The larger of two numbers. bit_and number, number number Bitwise and of two whole numbers; with bit_or , a way to track which of several items a subtree has used. bit_or number, number number Bitwise or of two whole numbers. bit_xor number, number number Bitwise exclusive or of two whole numbers. number_latex number text A number in LaTeX: a whole number as it is, a fraction as \frac{p}{q} with its sign in front. Generators ¶ Leaves that draw a whole number. They appear on the right of a production, or after random NAME = ; their arguments are whole numbers. A range may be of any width that fits in an integer, and integer(DIGITS) draws numbers of up to 18 digits. Function Takes Gives integer number number integer(n) : a whole number with exactly n digits. nonzero_integer number number nonzero_integer(n) : as integer , never 0. integer_between number, number number integer_between(a, b) : a whole number from a to b inclusive. nonzero_integer_between number, number number nonzero_integer_between(a, b) : as integer_between , never 0. Whole numbers ¶ Counting and number theory on whole numbers: factorials, binomial coefficients and permutations, greatest common divisors and least common multiples, powers and inverses modulo n. A result too large for a 63-bit integer, or an inverse that does not exist, stops generation with a message. Function Takes Gives base_digits number, number text base_digits(n, b) : the whole number n written in base b (2 to 16) as text, with the digits 0-9 and A-F. base_number number, number number base_number(n, b) : the number whose decimal digits are the digits of n in base b (2 to 10), so that eleven in binary is an answer typed as 1011 . factorial number number factorial(n) : n!, for n from 0 to 20. choose number, number number choose(n, k) : the number of ways to choose k of n; 0 when k is out of range. permutations number, number number permutations(n, k) : the number of ordered choices of k of n. gcd number, number number The greatest common divisor of two whole numbers. lcm number, number number The least common multiple of two whole numbers. pow_mod number, number, number number pow_mod(a, k, n) : the remainder of a^k on division by n, for k >= 0 and n > 0. mod_inverse number, number number mod_inverse(a, n) : the x in 0..n-1 with a x = 1 (mod n); an error unless a and n are coprime. Formulas ¶ Symbolic expressions in named variables: constants, the constant pi, variables, the four operations and powers, sin , cos , tan , exp , ln and sqrt , with differentiation, substitution, a zero test and LaTeX, and the exact values of sine, cosine and tangent at multiples of pi/6 and pi/4. A formula answer is graded by WeBWorK as a formula; one in variables other than x is written with a context that declares them. Function Takes Gives formula_constant number formula formula_variable text formula formula_add formula, formula formula formula_subtract formula, formula formula formula_multiply formula, formula formula formula_divide formula, formula formula formula_power formula, number formula formula_negate formula formula formula_sin formula formula formula_cos formula formula formula_tan formula formula formula_exp formula formula formula_ln formula formula formula_sqrt formula formula formula_substitute formula, text, formula formula differentiate formula, text formula differentiate(f, "x") : the derivative of formula f with respect to x . formula_latex formula text formula_is_zero formula truth value formula_pi nothing formula The constant pi, kept as a symbol: formula_multiply(formula_constant(5 / 6), formula_pi()) is written \frac{5\pi}{6} and graded as 5pi/6 . formula_value formula number The number a formula without variables comes to, exactly; an error when it holds a variable, pi or a value of a function that is not rational. exact_sin number, number formula exact_sin(p, q) : the value of sin(p pi / q) as a formula, such as sqrt(3)/2 , for multiples of pi/6 and pi/4; an error for other angles. exact_cos number, number formula exact_cos(p, q) : the value of cos(p pi / q), as exact_sin . exact_tan number, number formula exact_tan(p, q) : the value of tan(p pi / q), as exact_sin ; an error where the tangent is not defined. formula_to_polynomial formula, text polynomial Answers ¶ Functions that say how something is asked for, not what it is: an answer blank as part of a production's text, and an answer that must be worked out. Function Takes Gives matrix2 number, number, number, number matrix matrix3 number, number, number, number, number, number, number, number, number matrix matrix_identity number matrix matrix_add matrix, matrix matrix matrix_subtract matrix, matrix matrix matrix_multiply matrix, matrix matrix matrix_scale number, matrix matrix matrix_transpose matrix matrix matrix_determinant matrix number matrix_inverse matrix matrix matrix_is_invertible matrix truth value matrix_entry matrix, number, number number matrix_vector matrix, vector vector matrix_latex matrix text matrix_row_latex matrix, number text matrix_row vector matrix matrix_row(v) : the vector v as a matrix of one row. matrix_column vector matrix matrix_column(v) : the vector v as a matrix of one column. matrix_stack matrix, matrix matrix matrix_stack(A, B) : A above B ; they must have the same number of columns. matrix_augment matrix, matrix matrix matrix_augment(A, B) : A with B to its right, the augmented matrix [A | B] ; they must have the same number of rows. matrix_rows matrix number The number of rows of a matrix. matrix_columns matrix number The number of columns of a matrix. matrix_rank matrix number The rank of a matrix of any shape: the number of pivots of its reduced row echelon form. matrix_rref matrix matrix The reduced row echelon form of a matrix of any shape, with exact entries. matrix_null_space matrix matrix matrix_null_space(A) : the basis of the null space read off the reduced form, as the columns of a matrix: for each free variable in turn, the solution of A x = 0 in which it is 1 and the other free variables are 0.
